narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Drafting Room"**

A drafting room, not a dashboard. Patent drawings are the only pictures; everything around them is paper, ink and hairlines. Light mode is warm drafting paper, dark mode is graphite. Type is ink-black, there is one safety-orange accent for focus, links and selection, and filled actions are ink, not orange. The one place the patent-sheet idea shows is the drawing itself: a white sheet with a mono `FIG. 1` caption in its lower-left corner.

Three voices are kept apart by face. IBM Plex Sans is Patent Yard speaking (interface, headings, summaries, notes). IBM Plex Serif is the patent's own text (abstract, claims, description), so source text always reads differently from ours. IBM Plex Mono is every patent number, date, count and small label.

Working pages are left-aligned and dense: headings sit left with their action at the right edge, filters are grouped text buttons with micro-counters, card grids collapse into a ruled table, and data sits in hairline-divided cells instead of boxes. The visitor controls theme, drawing treatment in dark mode, text size and motion from the settings page.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper (light) and graphite (dark) grounds; ink type in three steps.
Hairlines (1px `line` / `line-strong`) do the structural work; shadows only for hover and floating layers.
Two radii: 6px for controls, 10px for panels, cards and drawings.
Status color is fixed site-wide and always paired with a word.
Drawings sit on a plate with a mono FIG caption; in dark mode the linework is inverted onto graphite unless the visitor asks for original white sheets.
One easing curve; every animation stops under reduced motion (OS or site setting).

rules.name: The Status Is Not The Accent Rule
rules.body: Orange means "you can act here" or "you are here"; status meaning comes only from the four status hues, and each badge carries its word.

rules.name: The Ink Fill Rule
rules.body: The filled primary action is ink, never orange. Orange stays rare enough to mark focus.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Sans for what Patent Yard writes, Serif for what the patent says, Mono for numbers and identifiers. A quoted claim in the sans, or a summary in the serif, is a bug.

rules.name: The Sans Metric Rule
rules.body: Big ledger numbers are sans with tabular figures, not mono; mono is for small numbers.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Containers rest flat with a hairline; a shadow is a state (hover) or a layer (floating).

dos: Do take every color from the CSS variables so light, dark and the settings page all follow.
Do put any new patent drawing on `plate` with the multiply/invert blend variables and a mono FIG caption.
Do set patent-quoted text in Plex Serif, numbers and dates in Plex Mono, and everything else in Plex Sans.
Do pair every status color with its word, and draw inferred status with the dashed edge.
Do divide data with hairlines inside one bordered container rather than boxing each value.
Do use 6px for controls and 10px for containers; nothing else.
Do honor both reduced-motion switches for any new animation.
donts: Don't use orange for status, or a status hue for actions.
Don't fill the primary button with the accent.
Don't add glows, gradient text, background grids, glass blur, corner brackets or fake window chrome.
Don't put shadows on resting containers.
Don't add pictures other than patent drawings.
